comment: The factory obligations register (0.9.0) — every forward-looking debt this release carries, in ONE machine-read home, read by scripts/check-obligations.mjs (clockless in lint.yml's machinery block; --clockful ONLY in hygiene.yml's scheduled job). The release's obligations previously lived in three unjoined sources — the ramp fleet (rampNote sites + template/migrations.json records), template/base/tools/deferrals.json, and prose — and gates-catalog.md's docs-sync section recorded the factory-side reader debt this register discharges.

Row schema: { id, kind: release|calendar|condition, target (x.y.z for release; YYYY-MM-DD for calendar; null for condition), sites?: [{file, mustContain?}] (prose anchors, ONE-WAY — the register is the index, the sites are anchors; the both-ways closure is the consumer scan's grammar and was the vacuous-port trap factory-side), reason (>= 40 chars), reviewedOn (YYYY-MM-DD), evidence (URL or repo file ref — REQUIRED for kind:condition) }.

Kinds: release reds CLOCKLESSLY when package.json reaches the target (check-ramp-ledger.mjs's version authority); calendar is judged ONLY under --clockful in the scheduled lane (a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR); condition NEVER reds on time — shape + evidence is its bar, and discharging one is DELETING it in a reviewed diff.

Unions the reader closes: every template/base/tools/deferrals.json entry id has a condition-or-release row here under the same id (the census); every shipped rampNote site whose `until` is still in the future has a kind:release row targeting its expiry version (the debt the next migrations record will owe, written down before it is due).

DELIBERATELY NOT LEDGERED: .harness/pending/source-fixes.json — it is CONSUMER-side, parked by `update` on the install and self-clearing via the probes in template/migrations.json seededSourceFixes (owned there, checked by scripts/check-seeded-migrations.mjs); a factory row would be a second, staler copy of a record that already has an owner.

obligations.reason: ASD opened consultation on 2026-06-15 to replace the Essential Eight with an ISM-grounded 'Essentials' series (Essentials for enterprise IT first), citing the cloud gap explicitly; reported at roughly 12 months to deprecation and 24 to retirement. Everything built against the E8 in 0.9.9 therefore has a bounded shelf life, and the stated reason for the change IS the product-versus-organisation mismatch tools/essential-eight.json documents. Judged in the scheduled lane only: a verdict that changes with the date must never red a PR. On arrival, re-verify against ASD and either re-date this row or retarget the register at the successor framework.

Essential Eight MFA-11, MFA-12 and MFA-14 require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication at ML3, and the platform cannot supply it today. TOTP is not phishing-resistant. Supabase WebAuthn MFA does produce aal2 (GoTrue IsAAL2Claim accepts mfa/webauthn) but is undocumented, absent from the Dashboard, marked @experimental in auth-js, challengeAndVerify is TOTP-only, and it is a billable add-on the CLI silently downgrades to false when cost is not confirmed. Passkeys are a SEPARATE aal1 primary sign-in system and do not satisfy it. This is a platform ceiling, not a schedule: it discharges when WebAuthn MFA ships documented and dashboard-reachable, by deleting this row and regrading the three requirements together.

Essential Eight MFA-01, MFA-04 and MFA-06 all say MFA "is used to authenticate" users or customers — a claim about ALL of them — and mandatory enrolment is NOT expressible in GoTrue: MFAConfiguration carries no Required field and there is no project-level require-MFA switch for end users. 0.9.9 shipped the enforcement half (the aal2 rail makes enrolment MEAN something: an enrolled user cannot reach the data with a password alone, on any surface) and deliberately not the enrolment surface, which needs a signup state machine and a challenge flow on both product surfaces. Until it exists, a user who never enrols authenticates with one factor and these rows stay not-implemented rather than being softened to alternate-control. Same shape as dsr-web-erase-surface: the rail exists, the surface is owed. ADR: docs/adr/20260812-mfa-aal2.md. RE-DATED TO 1.0.0 BY 0.10.0 on a CAPABILITY CEILING rather than on scope, and the distinction matters because a 0.11.0 date would be a promise nobody can keep: GoTrue’s MFAConfiguration carries no Required field and there is no project-level require-MFA switch for end users, so mandatory enrolment is not expressible on this platform at any date. What a release CAN build is the signup state machine and challenge flow on both surfaces, which is real work and does not by itself make the claim true — a user who never enrols still authenticates with one factor. It rides to 1.0.0 with the rest of the outcome-oracle work rather than being re-dated a minor at a time.

THE SCHEDULABLE HALF OF THE RETIRED e8-auth-event-logging. MFA-15 wants successful AND unsuccessful multi-factor authentication events centrally logged; verified against a running stack, a signup writes `user_signedup` and a sign-in writes `login`, but THREE FAILED SIGN-INS WRITE NOTHING AT ALL. RE-TARGETED FROM 0.11.0 TO 1.0.0, and the move is a correction of the 0.10.0 split rather than a slip: that row called this half 'BUILDABLE because the gap is in THIS repository rather than the platform', and walking the actual surfaces for 0.11.0 established that it is not buildable in the shape described. FOUR BLOCKERS, none previously recorded. (a) THE SCHEMA REFUSES THE ROW: audit.events carries `CONSTRAINT events_action_known CHECK (action IN ('INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE'))` in both the declarative schema and its migration, plus a NOT NULL org_id and table_name and an actor pinned to auth.uid() — a failed sign-in has no org, no table, and no uid, so 'write it into audit.events' is not a small addition but a change to the shape of the trail. (b) THERE IS NO SERVER-SIDE SIGN-IN SEAM to instrument on either surface; the web sign-in is deliberately client-side and its own source comments record why. (c) EVERY ANON-REACHABLE WRITER SHAPE IS ALREADY REFUSED by the rls-manifest closure and the security-definer allowlist — an unauthenticated endpoint that appends to the audit trail is also a write-amplification surface, and the limiter does not bind sign-in at all because that path goes to GoTrue. (d) MFA-15 IS ITS ONLY CITING ROW and cannot move regardless until e8-mfa-enrolment-surface, which is dated 1.0.0. A date this release could keep would have been a promise about a design nobody has. SHIPPED NOW INSTEAD, because it was actively misleading: docs/compliance/essential-eight.md told consumers to do the thing that the schema refuses.

Essential Eight RAP-20, RAP-21, AC-11, AC-12 and UAH-20 all turn on the word "centrally". The events this repository can produce ARE produced and ARE protected — audit.events is append-only in four layers and 0.9.9 added the elevated-role ATTEMPT (service_role trying to read, forge, modify, delete and truncate) rather than inferring refusal from a grant lookup, which is the difference between ASD's POOR and EXCELLENT evidence tiers. What no part of this repository can do is forward them: central logging means the record survives compromise of the system that produced it, and an in-database trail does not. THE FORWARDING HALF IS ASYMMETRIC AND MUST NOT BE GATED AS THOUGH IT WERE SYMMETRIC: one platform's log drains are API- and Terraform-addressable, the other's are Dashboard-only (verified negative against the live Management API specification — `drain` appears only as an enum value, never as a path). A gate resolving either from a live endpoint is refused outright by this repository's hermeticity rule (CONTRIBUTING: a gate that resolves its expectations from a live third-party endpoint turns an untouched commit red overnight, and this repo has already paid for that once). Retention is the other half of the reason: platform log retention tops out at 90 days by plan tier, so any requirement beyond that must ride a drain into a sink the operator controls. Discharge is a reviewed decision about WHERE the boundary sits, not a scheduled build. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work. IT ALSO ABSORBS MFA-16 (“event logs are protected from unauthorised modification and deletion”), which until 0.10.0 was owned by e8-auth-event-logging. The move is not filing convenience: auth.audit_log_entries carries zero non-internal triggers and `postgres` holds UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on it, and no append-only layer can be ADDED because the schema is GoTrue’s and GoTrue re-migrates it. So the only remedy for the protection requirement is the same act as the remedy for the forwarding ones — get a copy off the platform into a sink the operator controls — and two rows naming one remedy under two ids is how a ceiling gets discharged twice.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (RAP-20/21, AC-11/12, UAH-20, MFA-16): forwarding is not a build this repository

obligations.reason: Essential Eight RB-02 wants backups of data, applications AND settings synchronised to a common point in time. 0.9.9 shipped the evidence lane (`backup-evidence`, tools/check-backup-posture.mjs) and established that it does NOT discharge this row, for a reason worth recording rather than rediscovering: the platform's backup does not contain two of the three asset classes. Verified against the vendor's own pages — Edge Functions, Auth settings and API keys, Realtime settings, extensions and project settings, read replicas and Storage API objects all sit outside the database backup (the database holds only Storage metadata), and custom-role LOGIN passwords are stripped from it. The sharpest exclusion is the Vault/pgsodium root key: a backup carries ciphertext but never the key, so a restore into a NEW project cannot decrypt what it just restored until the key is carried across by hand — which is also the thing most likely to be discovered during a real recovery rather than before one. Discharge is a manifest that binds the database backup to the commit, the migration set and the deployed function versions, emitted at deploy time. Not built, and not scheduled: it needs a deploy-time artefact channel this repository does not yet have. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

obligations.reason: Essential Eight RB-03/RB-05/RB-06/RB-09 concern where backups live and who can reach them. 0.9.9 recorded what the vendor ATTESTS, labelled as attestation rather than as anything this system demonstrates: backups are AES-256 encrypted at rest with keys protected by FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs, stored in S3 on infrastructure independent of the project's own resources. That is a contractual statement in the data processing agreement, not an artefact any control here reads, so it cannot raise a grade. Two things remain unpublished and are recorded as unknowns rather than assumed either way: no storage region for backups is stated, and whether daily backups aging past the plan window (7 / 14 / 30 days) are DELETED or merely made inaccessible is never said — every statement takes the form "can access the last N days", which is an access claim and not a deletion one. RB-05/06/09 stay graded as they were, because "no client role can reach a backup" is true here only because this tree produces no backups of its own: vacuous truth, and the register's own rule is that absence of a surface is never a control. Discharge is a self-produced off-platform backup with its own store and IAM policy, which is an operator decision about where the boundary sits rather than a build to schedule. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (RB-03/05/06/09): the current grade rests on vacuous truth

obligations.reason: Essential Eight RB-11 requires backup administrator accounts to be prevented from modifying and deleting backups during the retention period. 0.9.9 re-verified the platform surface and the finding got SHARPER AND WEAKER AT THE SAME TIME, which is the point. Sharper: no Delete or Modify action for a backup appears anywhere — not as a row in the published permissions table, and not as any method across all 115 API paths. Weaker: that is an ABSENCE OF SURFACE, not a published control. Supabase nowhere states that backups cannot be deleted; it simply never offers the verb, and no page publishes an immutability, WORM or object-lock guarantee for the buckets holding them (searched: the backups guide, product security, the SOC 2 and HIPAA pages, the shared-responsibility model, the PITR usage page). Reading an unoffered verb as prevention would be exactly the inflation this register exists to refuse. There is also no backup-administrator role to separate: the four published roles are Owner, Administrator, Developer and Read-Only, the table grants backups only View/Download/Restore and PITR only View/Restore, `Developer` holds Download and Restore while being described as unable to change project settings, and `Read-Only` — the only role narrow enough to resemble a custodian — is denied both and is gated behind Team or Enterprise. ONE GAP IS EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIABLE AND MUST NOT BE GRADED IN EITHER DIRECTION: whether reducing the PITR recovery retention period, or removing the PITR add-on, destroys backup data already inside the previous window. The vendor documents the billing consequence and says the period can be changed, and publishes no data-lifecycle statement at all — which is the most plausible undocumented route by which a privileged account could destroy backups during their retention period, and precisely what this requirement asks about. Reachable only for self-produced off-platform dumps under S3 Object Lock in COMPLIANCE mode, which binds every principal including the account root. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (RB-11): an unoffered verb is not a control

obligations.reason: Essential Eight RAP-02 and RAP-03 require privileged access to be disabled after 12 months unless revalidated and after 45 days of inactivity. Neither exists: role_rank membership is a standing grant with no expiry and no inactivity sweep. Both windows are ASD's own verbatim numbers and are the only ones that may be encoded. RE-TARGETED TO 0.12.0 BY 0.11.0, AND THE PRECONDITION IT WAITED ON IS NOW SHIPPED rather than merely described. The blocker found while planning this release: check-tenancy.mjs resolved SQL functions FIRST-WINS (`functions.find` over migration order) while policies folded last-wins, so a `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION private.member_ranks()` — which is exactly the shape this discharge takes — would have been judged against the 2026-02-01 definition and the whole change would have been VACUOUS AT THE GATE: green on a migration whose rank ladder could be inverted. 0.11.0 fixes that fold (`resolveFunction`, the single home for the rule, with a red-proof that fails against the old resolution), so 0.12.0's migration lands against a gate that can actually see it. What remains unchanged is the cost: it touches the RLS admin predicate and therefore schema-rls, tenancy, migrations, db-limits, types-drift, contracts and the turn-fatal Stop step rls-isolation, which needs a live Supabase. One migration or neither.

Essential Eight RAP-13 requires just-in-time administration. Nothing in this tree elevates temporarily: role_rank is a standing grant and no admin session carries an expiry. Discharge is a time-bounded elevation whose expiry the RLS admin predicate actually CONSULTS, so an expired session stops satisfying it rather than merely being marked expired. RE-TARGETED TO 0.12.0 BY 0.11.0 on the same shipped precondition as e8-privilege-lifecycle — the check-tenancy function fold, which until 0.11.0 judged a redefined helper by its FIRST definition and would have passed this discharge without seeing it. One migration or neither: separated, `last_privileged_at` loses its only writer and RAP-03 degrades to an alternate control.

Essential Eight PA-11 (online services), PA-13 (applications) and POS-16 (operating systems) require products no longer supported by vendors to be removed or replaced. 0.9.9 DISCHARGED PA-13 and disproved the plan’s assumption that one artefact would cover all three. The built closure reads the npm registry’s own `deprecated` flags out of the RESOLVED pnpm-lock.yaml (a committed third-party artefact, so the check is hermetic), dispositions every one of them in the reviewed tools/eol.json, and RECOMPUTES each row’s production-vs-development scope from the lockfile instead of believing it — which on its first run disproved the note about to be written, since five of the scaffold’s six deprecated packages are development-only and uuid@7 is not (it arrives through expo -> @expo/config-plugins -> xcode). WHAT IS STILL OWED IS THE OTHER TWO ROWS, and neither is a scheduling matter. PA-11 wants ONLINE SERVICES: Supabase, Vercel, GitHub Actions, the npm registry, EAS. None of them has a support flag in any artefact this tree contains, and asking their APIs is refused by the hermeticity rule in CONTRIBUTING. POS-16 wants PLATFORMS: the CI runner image, the Node major, the Postgres major, the mobile target SDKs. store-policy.json holds currency floors, which assert recency and not vendor support, and POS-15 already claims framework-floor.json plus the version-sync step as its runtime-currency alternate control — so grading POS-16 on the same artefact would double-count one control across two requirements. Discharge for both is a reviewed per-service and per-platform support register with its own freshness window, or an honest permanent ceiling; it is a decision about where the boundary sits, not a build to schedule. CONVERTED release/0.10.0 -> condition in 0.10.0, and the conversion is deliberately the HEAVIER bill: a condition row needs `evidence`, but check-obligations.mjs accepts any URL unresolved and any repo path that merely exists, so this row also carries a sites[] anchor byte-checking the exact ceiling sentence in design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md — which the dated row never had to pay. NO OUTCOME CHANGES: every requirement naming this row stays not-implemented. What was false was the DATE, which asserted somebody could schedule the work.

sites.mustContain: CEILING (PA-11, POS-16): no support flag exists in any artefact this tree contains

obligations.reason: Essential Eight PA-06, PA-07 and PA-10 carry ASD's verbatim 48-hour, two-week and one-month windows for applying vendor mitigations, and no control measures advisory-publication against deployment time. framework-floor.json is clockless and offline by design: it holds a version floor, not a window. Discharge must encode ONLY ASD's stated numbers — the assessment guidance sets no window for 'in a timely manner', and inventing a 24- or 72-hour SLA would manufacture a contractual obligation with no framework backing. RE-DATED TO 1.0.0 BY 0.10.0, and it shares its blocker with e8-restore-manifest — which 0.10.0 converted to a condition row for exactly this reason. Both need a DEPLOY-TIME artefact channel: something emitted when the system is deployed, binding what shipped to when. This repository has no such channel, and inventing one is not a compliance task but an infrastructure one. Kept as a dated row rather than converted to a condition because unlike the restore manifest this one becomes schedulable the moment the channel exists, and 1.0.0 is where that work sits.

The standing ask-the-CLI config census is blocked UPSTREAM, not on scheduling: no Supabase CLI subcommand parses config.toml without side effects (config push needs a project ref, functions list needs a token, status binds to whichever stack holds the default ports and prints SECRET_KEY/JWT_SECRET). RE-CHECKED at the 0.10.0 arrival (2026-08-13) against the first real pin bump the standing rule has met — the catalog's `supabase: ^2.34.3` range now resolves to 2.114.0 (GA 2026-08-12) rather than the 2.113.0 both prior re-checks read. The CLI became a pnpm/nx monorepo and the Go CLI moved to apps/cli-go, but apps/cli-go/cmd/config.go AT TAG v2.114.0 still registers `push` alone, and supabase/cli#5894 is still open with no milestone and no linked PR. The consumer deferral entry carries the full re-check record and the standing per-arrival rule; this row is its census twin — it discharges only when the side-effect-free subcommand actually ships, by deleting both together.

THE DATED FACTS THIS HARNESS DEPENDS ON MOST HAVE NO SCHEDULED FRESHNESS CONTROL, and this row is the standing re-verification obligation that stands in for one. RE-VERIFIED AT 1.0.0 (2026-08-15) against Claude Code 2.1.232 / SDK 0.3.232, by the file's own method rather than by reading: the payload probe re-armed in .claude/settings.local.json (Facts 1/2/3 re-observed — SubagentStop's 14-key payload is key-for-key identical, last_assistant_message untruncated, verdict on the last non-empty line), the torn-hook exit-code matrix re-probed empirically (Fact 12 — identical: every load failure exits 1/fail-open, malformed stdin on an intact hook exits 2), the advisory surface re-queried (Fact 10 — same 28 advisories, floor unchanged at 2.1.163, checkedOn moved), the CI-spawn grep re-run (Fact 5 — still zero), and the hook environment re-captured (Fact 6 — two ADDITIVE deltas: CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET/TOKEN now reach hooks, the token is credential-shaped; CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 again observed in a MAIN session, re-confirming that a depth-cap control keyed on it would brick reviewer spawns). Fact 4's Stop-side payload was re-captured at the following turn end (key-for-key identical, stop_hook_active false, no agent_* fields); NOT RE-RUN: the one-shot stop_hook_active=true transition (it requires deliberately blocking a turn — the 2026-08-07 observation stands, at the original version, and the file says so in place); Facts 7/8/9/11/13 are documentation-sourced and were re-read, not probed. WHY THE ROW SURVIVES ITS OWN DISCHARGE CLAUSE: deleting it on a completed re-probe would recreate the no-freshness-control defect it names the next time Claude Code moves — the honest shape is a RECURRING re-verification row (the auth-posture-cli-census precedent), re-dated at each pass, whose first sites[] anchor pins the CURRENT re-verification date so the next re-observation must move this row in the same diff. A scheduled prober stays refused while Fact 5 holds: a prober needs a live Claude Code session in CI, and 'no CI lane spawns Claude' is a deliberate posture, not an accident to fix.

The suppressions census (inline-disable/escape-comment accounting) ships as a NEW chain step, and a new step is PRICED, not free — the injection inventory is unchanged and is enumerated in the 0.10.0 record: a configSteps record, the chain-budget row FIRST, the injections.json canary, the enforcement-tiers row, the validate.floor.json regen, the AGENTS.md gate-list escape, the check-docs-sync fixture move, the upgrade lane's leg-A doctrine flip, and a chain-budget re-record before ANY published figure. RE-TARGETED TO 0.12.0 BY 0.11.0. THE 0.10.0 ARGUMENT IS NOT REPEATED, because it no longer applies and saying so is the point: 0.10.0 deferred on the ground that no release in this lineage had combined a chain-step injection with a real expiry wave, and 0.11.0 carries the LARGEST wave the lineage has produced — five ramps across twelve vintages — so that argument now points at this release exactly as it did at the last one, and a reason that survives every release is not a reason. THE ACTUAL NEW INFORMATION IS THE COST OF THE RE-RECORD, and it is a CI dependency rather than a scope judgement: the committed 34/10 chain-budget measurement is what licenses the wall-clock figures published in README.md, `check-claims` reds on a published figure with no committed measurement behind it, and the re-record runs ONLY through the reviewed workflow_dispatch path. So an injection cannot be completed inside a working tree at all — it needs a dispatched measurement landed and committed before the release that grows the chain may publish a figure. Batching both steps into one release pays that CI round trip ONCE rather than twice, which is why this row and resilience-chain-step now share a target. CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD: the 0.10.0 reason specified re-opening the AGENTS.md gate-list escape 'at minVersion 0.10.0'. That is stale — an escape opened at a minVersion at or below the population it protects is inert for exactly that population — and the correct value is the version that injects the step.

The resilience closure (retry/timeout/backoff posture over the seams that call out) is the second chain step, paying the SAME priced injection inventory as suppressions-chain-step — one inventory, two steps, one chain-budget re-record after both land and before any published figure. RE-TARGETED TO 0.12.0 BY 0.11.0 ON A FACT 0.10.0 COULD NOT STATE, established by walking the seams this gate would judge: the shipped lint config (eslint.config.mjs) and the shipped documentation (docs/harness/README.md, docs/harness/gates-catalog.md) both describe an `apps/mobile/src/lib/api-client.ts` one-door and an `src/lib/sse.ts` streaming client, and NEITHER FILE EXISTS anywhere under template/. A gate whose whole subject is the posture of the outbound seams cannot be authored on top of a tree whose own configuration and prose disagree with it about which seams exist — the register would be written against files, the checker would scan a tree without them, and the closure would pass vacuously in precisely the way this repository deletes checks for. Reconciling that divergence is the prerequisite, it is a separate reviewed act from the step, and it is now the first half of this row. The 0.10.0 statement that 'the subject does not exist yet' was right in substance and understated the reason: the subject does not exist AND the tree claims it does.

The enterprise-facing controls crosswalk + threat model is GENERATABLE — harness.config.mjs (the chain), the guard-rules tables (the hooks), and tests/canary/injections.json (the proofs) are the three machine-read inputs — but it is gated on the licensing/wholeness decision design/CONFORMANCE-FACTS.md records for the conformance map: built whole against Annex I directly, or not at all, because a claimed level with an unmapped requirement is worse than no claim.

sites.mustContain: What this deliberately does NOT solve

obligations.reason: The 0.9.5 e2ee rails DECLARE three ports with no implementations — RecipientWrapPort (org sharing: an org-mate's RLS-visible row is ciphertext they cannot open), RecoveryPort (a lost device is lost data; WebCrypto ships no Argon2 and PBKDF2-as-the-KDF would be a dishonest default), and DeviceSyncPort (a second device has no path to the root key). Condition, not a dated row: each needs a design decision the harness should not date on a consumer's behalf, and the honest state is a declaration plus a stated loss rather than a promise. This row anchors the declarations to the README section that states their cost, so an implementation cannot quietly turn a declared port into a claim without the register moving too. Also open by construction: the web KeystoreAdapter returns raw bytes, which forecloses a non-extractable CryptoKey handle, and the keyring exports no rewrap primitive so key rotation is a full client-side re-encryption pass.

crypto-primitives-one-door matches a `crypto.subtle` member chain and NAMED cipher imports, and an adversarial review showed it misses the namespace routes: `import { webcrypto } from 'node:crypto'` then webcrypto.subtle.*, a default or `* as` import used as nodeCrypto.createCipheriv(...), and `const c = require('node:crypto')` followed by c.createCipheriv(...). Each needs binding-level tracking (which local names alias the module) rather than the single-node test the rule does now, and a half-tracked version would red honest code. The compensating controls are the mobile cipher-library one-door, the weak-crypto-algorithm write-guard, and the security reviewers on the crypto trigger paths.

A census entry's `module` value is validated as a non-empty string and never against the real module set, so a typo'd module name parks the stale arm PERMANENTLY dormant while the entry still pre-authorises a ./client barrel and a mobile runtime dependency — the silent widening the stale arm exists to prevent. The module list is canonical and readable (installer/lib/layout.mjs MODULES, template/modules/*), but the gate ships to consumers where neither path is guaranteed present, so the check needs a shipped list rather than a factory import. Condition until that list has a home.

The architecture-reviewer's trigger (0.9.5) is scoped to packages/** plus the two structural registers, deliberately NOT apps/** — the triggers file's own doctrine is narrowness first, because an over-matching trigger makes every diff owe every reviewer and gets routed around. Condition: widen to apps/*/lib/** (the web seam files) only once a release of reviewer-ledger evidence shows the packages-scoped trigger earns its verdicts rather than producing noise; the evidence is the .harness/reviewer-ledger.jsonl population at the widening review.

The full Stop chain executes off-Linux nowhere: the blocker is the DATABASE, not the shell — rls-isolation needs the live Supabase stack (Docker), which the Windows/macOS runners do not carry, while the gate/hook LOGIC is already proven cross-platform by the Windows unit matrix. Condition: discharge needs a supported off-Linux local-stack story upstream, re-checked at every Supabase CLI pin bump, not a date this repo can set.

The mutation critical-surface definition (tools/lib/mutation-critical.mjs, shared by the PR diff-scoper and the nightly) is harness-OWNED while every file it names is SEEDED — a consumer whose tree diverges from the exemplar paths silently mutates less than the lane claims.
